backup.noApps: No apps to back up yet.
backup.restoreLead: These folders are replaced with their content from {time}, and the app is started from the compose file of that moment. What changed since then is lost.
backup.appLead: A snapshot holds the compose file, the app's folders in AppData and its Docker volumes — and the other folders you choose. The app is stopped while it is copied.
backup.noDir: The folder is created with the first snapshot
backup.enableHint: Each app is stopped for the time it takes to copy it.
backup.dirHint: Best on another disk. Empty — Backups in the data folder.
backup.beforeUpdateHint: So an update that went wrong can be undone.
backup.how: Snapshots are plain tar.gz files: they can be copied elsewhere and unpacked by hand.
error.settings.badBackup: The backup settings are not valid.
error.settings.badBackupDir: The backup folder must be an absolute path.
auth.codeHint: Six digits, or one of your recovery codes.
account.passwordChanged: The password is changed. Other devices were signed out.
twofa.title: Two-factor sign-in
twofa.onHint: Signing in asks for a code from your authenticator app. Recovery codes left: {n}.
twofa.offHint: Add a code from an app on your phone to the password.
twofa.setupLead: Scan the code with an authenticator app, then enter the six digits it shows.
twofa.secret: Or enter this key by hand
twofa.recoveryLead: Each code signs you in once if you lose your phone. They are shown only now.
twofa.turnOffLead: Signing in will need only the password again.
users.roleHint: A member sees the apps and opens them. A guest is a shared account that opens only the apps it is given. An administrator manages the server.
users.passwordHint: At least 8 characters. The user can change it after signing in.
users.setPasswordLead: The user is signed out everywhere and signs in with the new password.
users.rolesHint: Members see the apps and open them; guests open only the apps they are given. Neither can install, change or remove anything.
error.auth.forbidden: Only an administrator can do this.
error.totp.wrongCode: The code is wrong. Check that the phone's clock is right.
error.users.nameTaken: A user with this name already exists.
error.users.lastAdmin: The last administrator cannot be removed or demoted.
account.guest: This is a shared guest account. Its password is managed by an administrator.
invite.title: You are invited to this server
invite.lead: Choose a name and a password. You will join as: {role}.
invite.invalid: It was already used, has expired or was withdrawn. Ask for a new one.
invite.newLead: The link works once and for seven days. Whoever opens it chooses their own name and password.
invite.linkLead: Send it to the person. It is shown only now.
signins.title: Sign-in log
access.title: Who can open what
access.onlyHidden: hidden in Hata only — the port is open
access.others: Other ports stay open. Tick the ones that are web pages to ask for sign-in there too:
access.cannot.noPort: This app has no web port to guard.
access.cannot.hostNetwork: This app uses the host's network, so its port cannot be taken over.
access.how: With sign-in in front, Hata takes over the app's port and lets through only people who are signed in to Hata and allowed to open the app; the address stays the same. Without it, a limit only hides the app in Hata. Administrators can always open everything. Sign-in stands in front of the app's web port; its other ports stay open unless ticked, and only a port that serves web pages can be guarded.
error.invite.invalid: The invitation link does not work any more.
error.gate.noPort: This app has no web port to guard.
error.gate.hostNetwork: This app uses the host's network, so its port cannot be taken over.
error.gate.noFreePort: No free local port was found for the app.
error.gate.badAccess: The access list is not valid.
https.mode.proxy: Behind my own proxy (nginx, Caddy, Traefik)
https.mode.acme: HTTPS by Hata, certificate from Let's Encrypt
https.explain.off: Hata and the apps are opened by the server's address and ports over plain HTTP. Fine inside a home network.
https.explain.proxy: Your proxy holds the certificate and passes requests to Hata over HTTP. Point the domain and *.domain at this server's port, keep the Host header and send X-Forwarded-Proto. Hata then believes the proxy's headers, so do not let others reach its port directly.
https.explain.acme: Hata listens on ports 80 and 443 and gets a certificate for its name and for each app's name from Let's Encrypt. The names must lead to this server from the internet.
https.domainHint: The name of Hata itself. Each app gets its own: app.domain.
https.checking: Asking the domain for this server…
https.checkLead: Hata opens https://{domain} and a made-up app address the way a browser would, and looks whether the request comes back to it, over HTTPS, with the name kept.
https.addressesLead: Each app with a web page has an address of its own. An app behind Hata's sign-in asks for it here too.
error.settings.badHttps: The HTTPS settings are not valid.
error.settings.badEmail: This does not look like an email address.
https.certificatesLead: One per name, renewed a month before it expires. A name must lead to this server's port 80 for the certificate authority to confirm it.
https.needPort80: Hata listens on port {port}, but the certificate authority checks names on port 80. Move Hata to port 80: sudo hata install --port 80
import.title: Bring in what already runs
import.lead: Containers on this machine that are not apps of Hata yet. Once taken in, they get a tile, updates, backups and sign-in like any other app.
import.nothing: Nothing to bring in: every container on this machine is already an app here.
import.projectsHint: Started with docker compose somewhere else
import.taken: {name} is now an app of Hata.
import.source.file: Hata copies this compose file and manages the same containers from now on. Nothing is restarted; the original file stays where it is and is no longer used.
import.source.resolved: The project's file depends on where it lies (relative paths, its own variables), so Hata keeps it written out in full, as compose reads it today. Nothing is restarted; the original files stay where they are.
import.source.containers: The project's compose file was not found on this machine, so this one is written from its running containers. They keep running as they are and are recreated from this file at the next start or update — on the same volumes.
import.containerLead: This compose file is written from the container's settings. Check it, change what you like — it becomes the app's file.
import.step.stop: Container {name} is stopped and set aside.
import.step.start: The app is started from this file, with the same folders and volumes — no data is copied or deleted.
import.step.remove: When it is up, the old container is removed.
import.step.undo: If it does not come up, the old container is put back as it was.
import.warn.links: The container uses --link to reach another container. A compose file cannot say that: put both on one network instead, or the link is lost.
import.warn.volumesFrom: The container takes volumes from another container (--volumes-from). They are written here as its own volumes; check the list.
import.warn.sharedNetwork: The container shares the network of another container. That is left out of the file: add network_mode: "service:…" or "container:…" by hand.
import.problem.badName: Its name cannot be an app name
import.problem.exists: An app with this name exists
import.casaos.title: CasaOS: apps to move in — {n}
import.casaos.lead: Hata takes CasaOS's apps over where they are: the same compose files, the same folders, the same ports. Containers keep running, nothing is copied or deleted, and CasaOS stays installed.
import.casaos.stopHint: Its dashboard and services are stopped and disabled so that two managers do not run the same apps: {units}
error.import.notFound: It is no longer there, or it is already an app.
error.import.autoRemove: This container was started with --rm: it disappears when stopped, so there is nothing to rebuild.
update.title: Update {title}
update.lead: The {store} store has a newer version. This is what changes in the app's compose file; what you changed yourself stays.
update.guessed: This app was installed before Hata kept the store's original file, so only your ports, folders and variable values are known to be yours. Anything else edited by hand follows the store — check the list.
update.matched: This app does not say where it came from; the {store} store has an app of the same name. Only its ports, folders and variable values are kept; anything else follows the store — check the list.
update.conflictsLead: You and the store changed the same thing. Your value stays; the store's new value is shown under it.
update.file: The compose file after the update
error.app.noUpdate: The store has no newer version of this app.
attention.update.title: Hata {version} is available
attention.update.text: A newer version can be installed from Settings → About.
update.availableHint: Downloaded from GitHub and checked before it replaces this version. Apps keep running; if the new version does not start, this one comes back.
update.manual: This Hata does not run as the installed service, so it cannot replace itself. Run the installer again to update.
update.upToDate: This is the newest version. Checked {time}.
update.rolledBack: Hata {version} did not start on this machine, so the previous version was put back.
error.update.unsupported: This Hata does not run as the installed service and cannot replace itself.
error.update.running: An update is already being installed.
passkey.title: Passkeys
passkey.lead: Sign in with this device's fingerprint, face or PIN instead of the password. A passkey replaces the password and the two-factor code at once.
passkey.needDomain: Passkeys work when Hata is opened by its domain name over HTTPS: browsers do not offer them on a plain address. Set a domain in Settings → HTTPS and domain, then open Hata by that name.
passkey.addLead: A passkey signs in without the password, so adding one asks for it. After that your device will ask to confirm it is you.
passkey.name: Name
passkey.nameHint: So that you can tell your devices apart later.
error.passkey.unavailable: Passkeys work only when Hata is opened by its domain name over HTTPS.
error.passkey.tooMany: Too many passkeys: remove one you no longer use.
files.truncated: This folder holds more than is shown here.
files.dropHint: Drop files or folders here, or press Upload.
files.sort.name: By name
files.col.name: Name
files.deleteLead: Files: {files}, folders: {dirs}, {size} in total. They go to the trash and can be put back from there.
trash.title: Trash
trash.lead: What is deleted in Files lies here for {days} days, on the disk it was on, and can be put back where it was. After that it is removed for good. Until then it takes up room on its disk.
trash.emptyLead: Everything in it — {n} items, {size} — is deleted for good and cannot be put back.
trash.deleteLead: It cannot be put back after that.
files.deleteAppData: This is an app's own data. Without it the app may lose its settings or stop working.
error.files.protected: The server stands on this: it cannot be changed, renamed, moved or deleted here.
error.files.notFound: It is not there any more.
error.files.badName: A name cannot be empty, “.” or “..”, and cannot contain “/”.
error.files.samePlace: It is already in this folder.
error.files.intoItself: A folder cannot go into itself.
error.files.uploadOrder: The upload broke off. Try once more.
error.files.tooLargeToEdit: The file is too large to edit here (over {max} MB). Download it instead.
error.files.notText: This is not a text file.
error.files.changed: The file was changed by someone else meanwhile. Open it again.
error.files.archiveTooLarge: Too much for one archive (over 3.8 GB or 60 000 entries). Download it in parts.
error.files.noTrash: “{name}” lies on a disk that keeps no trash ({code}): it can only be deleted for good.
error.files.readOnlyDisk: This disk is read-only: nothing on it can be changed.
error.files.virtual: These are the kernel's own files (/proc, /sys, /dev): they can be listed, not read or changed.
error.files.tooManyPinned: The dashboard holds {max} folders at most. Remove one first.
home.badLink: An address starts with http:// or https://
home.emptyGroup: Nothing here yet — drag tiles in.
home.dragOut: Drag a tile outside to take it out.
home.addHint: An app, a link or a folder
home.addLinkHint: Any address: the router, a camera, a site
home.addFolderHint: A folder of this server, opened in Files
terminal.title: Terminal
terminal.hostHint: A shell on this server. It keeps running when the page is closed.
terminal.confirmNew: End this shell and everything running in it, and start a new one?
terminal.limit: Too many terminals are open. Close one of them first.
error.terminal.notRunning: The app is not running: there is no container to open a terminal in.
appearance.accentHint: Buttons, links and what is selected.
appearance.backgroundHint: A light colour turns the whole page light. Without one, the page follows the system.
appearance.dimHint: More of it makes text easier to read.
error.appearance.tooLarge: The picture is too large: {max} MB at most.
error.appearance.notImage: This is not a picture Hata can show: JPEG, PNG, WebP or AVIF.
backup.serverHint: Hata's settings, users, the dashboard and the apps' compose files. It is made with every run; together with the snapshots of the apps below it is the whole server.
backup.serverRestore: To bring the server back on a new machine: install Hata, put this folder with the backups there and run
backup.serverDone: The server's state is backed up
activity.system.restore.done: Server restored from a backup: {target} apps
home.addGroupHint: A named section of the dashboard
home.layoutTextHint: Everything on the dashboard, to edit by hand
home.layoutTextLead: Groups, tiles and where every block stands, as YAML. What does not fit a layout is dropped on saving.
error.dashboard.badText: This text is not a layout: {message}
local.title: Name on the home network
local.lead: Hata answers to a name on your home network, so nobody has to remember the address. Each app with a web page gets a name of its own under it.
local.enabledHint: Hata and the apps are opened by name as well as by address.
local.name: Name
local.nameHint: A name ending in .local Hata answers for itself (mDNS): nothing is set up on phones, computers or the router. Any other name, like hata.lan, has to be added to your router's DNS.
local.apps: Each app with a web page has a name of its own, like {example}. Open Hata by its local name and the tiles lead there.
error.settings.badLocalName: A name is letters, digits and hyphens: one word (hata) or words with dots between them (hata.lan).
local.otherLead: Only names ending in .local are found without a DNS server. Add two records to the DNS of your router: {domain} and *.{domain}, both leading to {address}.
local.unknown: the DNS this server uses does not know the name
notify.lead: What the home page lists under "Needs attention" can also reach you where you are: on your devices, in Telegram, through ntfy or a webhook.
notify.problemsHint: An app that keeps restarting, a failed backup or update, a disk filling up, a new version of Hata. Each problem is sent once, after it has lasted a minute and a half.
notify.lastError: The last message ({time}) was not delivered: {message}
notify.push.title: Devices
notify.push.lead: A notification from the browser or from Hata installed as an app, on this phone or computer. Each administrator switches it on for their own devices.
notify.pushNeedsHttps: Browsers allow notifications only on a page opened over HTTPS. Set a domain in Settings → HTTPS and domain, open Hata by it — and this device can be switched on here. Telegram, ntfy and a webhook work without it.
notify.pushUnsupported: This browser cannot receive notifications. On an iPhone or iPad, add Hata to the home screen first (Share → Add to Home Screen) and open it from there.
notify.denied: Notifications are blocked for this page in the browser — allow them in the site's settings and try again.
notify.telegram.title: Telegram
notify.telegram.lead: Messages from a bot of your own: create one with @BotFather, paste its token here, and write anything to the bot from the chat that should get the messages.
notify.telegram.chatHint: The number of the chat, or @name of a channel. "Find" lists the chats that wrote to the bot lately.
notify.telegram.noChats: Nobody has written to this bot lately. Send it any message and press "Find" again.
notify.ntfy.title: ntfy
notify.ntfy.lead: A topic on ntfy.sh or on an ntfy server of your own; the ntfy app on the phone shows what arrives.
notify.ntfy.urlHint: The server and the topic, like https://ntfy.sh/my-topic. Whoever knows the topic's name can read it — pick one that cannot be guessed.
notify.webhook.title: Webhook
notify.webhook.lead: A POST request with JSON (title, text, severity, code, app, url, server, time) to an address of yours — for n8n, Home Assistant, a script.
notify.test.title: A test from Hata
error.notify.bad: These notification settings cannot be saved.
error.notify.badToken: This does not look like a bot token: it is a number, a colon and a long string.
error.notify.badChat: The chat is a number (it can start with a minus) or @name of a channel.
error.notify.needTelegram: Telegram needs both the bot token and the chat.
error.notify.badNtfy: The topic address has to be a web address ending in the topic's name, like https://ntfy.sh/my-topic.
error.notify.badUrl: The address has to start with http:// or https://.
error.notify.badSubscription: The browser gave a subscription Hata cannot use.
error.notify.tooManyDevices: Too many devices are subscribed — remove the ones no longer used.
error.notify.telegramRefused: Telegram did not accept this token (or the bot is set to deliver its updates to a webhook).
edit.lead: The app's compose file as a form. What the form does not show stays in the file as it is; comments in the file are not kept. The Compose tab has the whole file.
edit.broken: The compose file of this app cannot be read as YAML — fix it on the Compose tab.
edit.title: Title
edit.webUiHint: Where the tile leads when Hata is opened by its address: the address, the port and the path. Leave the address empty for this server and the port empty for an app without a page.
edit.webDomainHint: The app's own address when Hata is opened by its domain: {names}. Hata leads it to the port above. Leave it empty for the app's name.
edit.webDomainElsewhere: Not used while the address above names another machine: the tile leads there.
edit.volumesHint: A folder of the server (an absolute path) or the name of a Docker volume, and where the container sees it.
edit.rawHint: Written in a way the form has no fields for; it stays as it is unless taken out. Change it on the Compose tab.
edit.privilegedHint: Gives the container nearly everything the server itself may do.
store.customFormLead: Describe the container the way CasaOS asks for it; Hata writes the compose file.
error.edit.invalid: The form was not filled in the way the server expects — reload the page and try again.
error.edit.badImage: Give the Docker image, like nginx:alpine.
error.edit.badPort: A port is a number from 1 to 65535; the container's port is required.
error.edit.badVolume: A volume needs a folder of the server (an absolute path) or a volume name, and an absolute path in the container.
error.edit.badEnv: A variable needs a name made of letters, digits and underscores.
error.edit.sameEnv: The same variable is listed twice.
error.edit.badDevice: A device is a path on the server, like /dev/ttyUSB0, and a path in the container.
error.edit.badCapability: Capabilities are names like NET_ADMIN, separated by commas.
error.edit.badIcon: The icon has to be a web address starting with http:// or https://.
error.edit.badWeb: The Web UI address is a host name, a port from 1 to 65535 and a path.
error.edit.badDomain: The name under the domain is one word of Latin letters, digits and hyphens, up to 63 characters.
error.edit.domainTaken: The app {app} already answers to this name. Choose another one.
error.edit.badService: A service needs a name of its own made of letters, digits, - and _, and an app needs at least one service.
run.title: Fill in from a docker run command
run.lead: Paste the command from the app's instructions. It is only read into the form — nothing is started until you install.
run.ignored: These options have no field in the form and were left out — add them on the Compose tab afterwards if the app needs them:
error.run.notRun: This is not a docker run command.
edit.removeServiceLead: It leaves the form with everything set for it. Its container is stopped and removed once the form is saved; its folders and volumes stay.
edit.iconHint: The address of a picture, or a picture of your own: PNG, JPEG, WebP, AVIF or SVG, up to 1 MB.
edit.iconOwn: Your own picture is used; it is kept next to the app's compose file as icon.*. Remove it to go back to the address.
error.icon.tooLarge: The picture is too large: {max} MB at most.
error.icon.notImage: This is not a picture Hata can show: PNG, JPEG, WebP, AVIF or SVG.
state.title: Configuration folder
state.lead: Where Hata keeps what it knows: the settings, the users, the dashboard, and for every app its compose file and icon. The data of the apps is not here — that is the data folder above.
state.folderHint: To move it, type another folder — a new or an empty one — and press Move. Everything is copied there and Hata restarts; the apps keep running.
state.notMovable: It can be moved from here only when Hata runs as the installed service.
state.moveLead: Everything in {from} is copied to {to} and Hata restarts there — the page comes back in a few seconds. The apps keep running. The old folder is not deleted: it is put aside under a new name next to where it was.
state.inDataRoot: This is inside the data folder ({path}). An app that is given the whole data folder would also see Hata's users and sessions — choose a place apps do not reach if you can.
state.moving: Moving the configuration folder — Hata is restarting…
state.notBack: Hata has not come back yet. Reload the page in a moment; if it stays away, look at the service's log on the server.
error.state.badPath: Give an absolute path to a folder of your own — not the root and not a folder of the system.
error.state.nested: The new folder cannot be inside the current one, or hold it.
error.state.notEmpty: That folder is not empty. Choose a new one or an empty one.
error.state.busy: Something is being installed or changed right now — wait until it is done.
error.state.copyFailed: The folder could not be copied: {message}
error.state.notService: The configuration folder can be moved only when Hata runs as the installed service.
offsite.title: A copy on another machine
offsite.enable: Send every snapshot to another machine
offsite.enableHint: Over SFTP: a NAS, a rented storage box, another server. The backups here stay as they are; this is a second copy, for the day this machine is gone.
offsite.pathHint: Without a leading slash it starts at the user's home folder.
offsite.keyHint: Add this line to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys of {user} on the other machine. Hata signs in with this key, never with a password.
offsite.sealHint: Files are encrypted before they leave: the other machine cannot read them.
offsite.passphraseHint: Write it down somewhere else. Without it the copy cannot be opened — a restore on a new machine asks for it. Changing it applies to snapshots sent from then on.
offsite.denied: The other machine does not let Hata in: add Hata's key above to authorized_keys of that user, then save again.
offsite.noSftp: This machine has no sftp. Install the package openssh-client.
offsite.inStep: In step with this machine · checked {when}
offsite.hostLead: Hata sees this machine for the first time. It shows this key:
offsite.hostHint: To be sure nobody stands in between, compare it with what the machine itself prints for:
error.offsite.badHost: The address must be a host name or an IP address.
error.offsite.badPort: The port must be a number from 1 to 65535.
error.offsite.badUser: The user name may hold letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores.
error.offsite.badPath: The folder must not be empty or hold quotes, backslashes, *, ?, brackets or "..".
error.offsite.badPassphrase: The passphrase must be at least 8 characters.
attention.offsite.title: The copy of the backups on another machine is behind
activity.system.offsite.failed: Sending backups to another machine failed
disks.title: Disks
disks.lead: What each disk says about its own health (SMART), read every half an hour. A disk that sleeps is not woken for it.
disks.none: No disks are visible from here. Inside a container Hata sees only the file systems it was given.
disks.tool.missingHint: It is read with smartctl from the smartmontools package, which is not installed on this server.
disks.tool.denied: Hata may not open the disks
disks.tool.deniedHint: Reading SMART needs root on the machine itself; in a container the disks are usually out of reach.
disks.fs.title: File systems
disks.fs.lead: Where files are kept on this server, network folders included.
disks.noSmart: This disk gives no SMART data: a virtual disk, or a USB case that hides it.
disks.finding.failing: The disk itself reports that it is failing. Copy what matters off it now and replace it.
disks.finding.critical: The drive raised a critical warning. Copy what matters off it now and replace it.
disks.finding.spare: The drive is running out of spare blocks: {n}% left. Replace it.
disks.finding.test: The last self-test failed. Copy what matters off the disk and replace it.
disks.finding.reallocated: The disk has moved {n} damaged sectors to its spare area. It still works, but disks that start doing this fail more often — keep a second copy of what is stored only here.
disks.finding.pending: {n} sectors could not be read and wait to be moved. Keep a second copy and plan a replacement.
disks.finding.uncorrectable: {n} sectors hold data the disk could not recover. Keep a second copy and plan a replacement.
disks.finding.media: The drive failed to give data back {n} times. Keep a second copy and plan a replacement.
disks.finding.worn: The drive has used {n}% of the writes it is rated for. Plan a replacement.
disks.finding.hot: The disk is hot: {n} °C. Heat shortens its life — check the airflow around it.
disks.value.reallocatedHint: damaged and moved to the spare area
disks.value.uncorrectableHint: data the disk could not recover
disks.value.mediaHint: data the drive could not give back
disks.value.crcHint: a cable or a port, not the disk itself
disks.value.wearHint: of the writes the drive is rated for
disks.test.hint: The disk tests itself and stays usable meanwhile: a short test takes about two minutes, a long one reads the whole surface and takes hours.
fills.title: What fills {path}
fills.lead: The data folder measured once a day: its folders, each app's data and the trash. The pace is the change over the last week.
fills.never: Not measured yet. Hata measures the folder once a day, quietly; on a large folder the first time takes a few minutes.
fills.outsideHint: the system, Docker's images and everything else on this disk
mounting.title: Using this disk
mounting.formatHint: Erases the disk and makes a new file system on it.
mounting.absent: the disk is not connected now
mounting.foundHolds: It holds: {what}. Hata has not changed anything on it.
mounting.foundEmpty: It looks empty. Hata has not changed anything on it.
mounting.mergeLead: The disks ticked below show up as one folder that is as large as all of them together. A new file goes to the disk with the most free room; every file stays a plain file on one of the disks, readable there without Hata.
mounting.mergeWarn: This is room, not safety: there is no second copy, and a disk that fails takes the files that were on it. The disks stay connected on their own too, and the merged folder waits for all of them at start.
mounting.needs.mergerfs.what: What is missing: mergerfs, a small system package that shows several folders as one.
mounting.needs.mergerfs.why: What for: it is what puts the disks together; the files themselves stay ordinary files on each disk.
error.disk.badMerge: Choose at least two folders that Hata connected and that are in no merged folder yet.
error.disk.noMergeTool: The program that merges disks is not installed.
error.disk.holds.pool: This disk is part of a merged folder. Disconnect the merged folder first.
mounting.blocked.system: The system runs from this disk, so Hata will never erase it.
mounting.blocked.mounted: Something other than Hata has a part of this disk connected, so it cannot be formatted whole.
mounting.blocked.swap: The disk is in use as swap space.
mounting.blocked.member: The disk is part of an array, a volume group or an encrypted volume. Hata does not touch those.
mounting.formatErases: Everything on this disk will be erased, for good. It holds:
mounting.formatEmpty: The disk looks empty. Whatever is on it will be erased, for good.
mounting.formatPartErases: Everything on this partition will be erased, for good. The other partitions of the disk are not touched.
mounting.formatLeaves: It is connected as {paths} now: that folder is disconnected first.
mounting.fs.ext4: ext4 — for a disk that stays in this server
mounting.fs.exfat: exFAT — for a disk or a stick that goes to other devices
mounting.fsHint.ext4: Keeps owners and permissions of files, which apps need for their data. Windows and macOS do not read it.
mounting.fsHint.exfat: Windows, macOS, Linux, phones and televisions of today read and write it; files of any size. No owners or permissions.
mounting.fsHint.vfat: Read by nearly everything, old car stereos, printers and cameras included. No file larger than 4 GB, no disk over 2 TB.
mounting.fsHint.ntfs: The file system of Windows. macOS only reads it; televisions and phones often do not open it.
mounting.label: Label
mounting.labelHint.ext4: The name other devices show the disk under. Up to 16 characters; may be left empty.
mounting.labelHint.exfat: The name other devices show the disk under. Up to 11 characters, in any language.
mounting.labelHint.vfat: The name other devices show the disk under. Up to 11 capital Latin letters and digits.
mounting.labelHint.ntfs: The name other devices show the disk under. Up to 32 characters, in any language.
mounting.after.keep: Connect it and keep it connected
mounting.after.once: Connect it until it is unplugged
mounting.afterHint.keep: Written to /etc/fstab: the disk is there after every restart, and the server still starts when the disk is not.
mounting.afterHint.once: It shows up as a folder now, to copy files to; eject it here before unplugging.
mounting.afterHint.no: Nothing is connected: the disk can be unplugged as soon as this is done.
mounting.name: Name
mounting.nameHint: Latin letters, digits, dots, hyphens and underscores.
mounting.typeName: To confirm, type the disk's short name: {name}
mounting.passwordHint: Your Hata password: erasing a disk cannot be undone.
fsck.title: Check {name}
fsck.lead: Hata looks the file system over for damage — what an unplugging without ejecting or a power cut leaves behind. The check itself changes nothing; what it finds can be repaired afterwards.
fsck.leadMounted: The folder {path} is disconnected for the time of the check and connected again afterwards. Stop what is using it first.
fsck.ntfs: NTFS is checked in full only by Windows (chkdsk). Here the common damage is found and mended, and the mark “not closed properly”, with which the disk refuses to connect, is taken off.
fsck.running: Checking… A large disk takes a long time.
fsck.verdict.fixed: Repaired. Files that lost their folder, if there were any, now lie at the top of the disk (in “lost+found” on ext4).
fsck.verdict.errors: Damage found. Nothing has been changed yet.
fsck.verdict.failed: The check could not be finished — see what the program said.
fsck.back: The folder could not be connected again: {message}
relabel.title: Rename {name}
relabel.lead: The label is the name other devices show the disk under. The files are not touched, and the folder it is connected as stays the same.
relabel.leadMounted: The folder {path} is disconnected for a moment and connected again. Stop what is using it first.
mounting.readyLead: It is connected as {path}. Apps reach it by that path, and it can be shared over the network like any folder.
data.moveLead: Everything in {from} — the apps' data, media, backups kept there — is copied to the new folder, the apps are pointed at it, and so are the shared folders and the folders on the dashboard.
data.targetHint: A new or an empty folder, usually on a disk you have just connected.
data.moveWarn: The apps are stopped while the files are copied and started again afterwards; a large folder takes a long time. The old folder is not deleted: it is kept next to itself with “.moved” and the date in its name, for you to delete once everything works.
error.data.badPath: Give an absolute path to a folder of your own — not the root, not a folder of the system and not Hata's configuration.
error.data.samePath: The data folder is already there.
error.data.nested: The new folder cannot be inside the current one, or hold it.
error.data.notEmpty: That folder is not empty. Choose a new one or an empty one.
error.data.busy: Something is being installed or changed right now — wait until it is done.
error.data.isRoot: The data folder is the whole file system (/), which cannot be moved. Type the new folder in the field and save instead.
error.data.hasMounts: Another disk is connected inside the data folder: {paths}. Its files would be left behind — disconnect it or connect it elsewhere first.
error.data.noSpace: There is not enough free room in the new place for everything in the data folder.
error.data.ownerless: The file system of that disk ({fstype}) keeps no owners or permissions for files, and apps need them for their data. Format the disk as ext4 in Settings → Storage (that erases it) or choose another one.
mounting.connectLead: The files on it stay as they are: nothing is erased or changed. They show up as the folder below.
mounting.noOwners: A {fs} file system does not know owners and permissions: everything on it will be open for reading and writing to every app and every account of the server.
mounting.keep: Connect it again after a restart
mounting.keepHint: Written to /etc/fstab. Without this the disk stays connected until it is unplugged or the server restarts.
mounting.disconnectLead: The files stay on the disk. The folder disappears from the server and is no longer connected after a restart.
mounting.ejectLead: Hata finishes writing, disconnects the folder and switches the disk off. After that it is safe to unplug.
mounting.ejected: {path} is ejected. The disk can be unplugged.
mounting.automountHint: A USB disk with files on it shows up as /mnt/usb-<its label> a few seconds after it is plugged in, for reading and writing. Nothing on it is changed; eject it here before unplugging.
mounting.needs.ntfs-3g.what: What is missing: ntfs-3g, a small system package that reads and writes NTFS, the file system of Windows.
mounting.needs.ntfs-3g.why: What for: it makes, checks and names NTFS file systems, and opens them where this system's kernel cannot do it by itself.
mounting.needs.fdisk.what: What is missing: fdisk, a small system package with the sfdisk program, which writes a disk's partition table.
mounting.needs.fdisk.why: What for: a disk formatted whole gets a new partition table.
mounting.needs.sfdisk.what: What is missing: sfdisk, a small program that writes a disk's partition table.
mounting.needs.sfdisk.why: What for: a disk formatted whole gets a new partition table.
mounting.needs.util-linux.what: What is missing: util-linux, the system package with the sfdisk program, which writes a disk's partition table.
mounting.needs.util-linux.why: What for: a disk formatted whole gets a new partition table.
mounting.needs.e2fsprogs.what: What is missing: e2fsprogs, the system package that makes ext4 file systems.
mounting.needs.e2fsprogs.why: What for: it makes, checks and names ext4 file systems.
mounting.needs.dosfstools.what: What is missing: dosfstools, a small system package that makes, checks and names FAT file systems.
mounting.needs.dosfstools.why: What for: FAT32 is what old devices read.
mounting.needs.exfatprogs.what: What is missing: exfatprogs, a small system package that makes, checks and names exFAT file systems.
mounting.needs.exfatprogs.why: What for: exFAT is what sticks and disks that go between devices carry.
mounting.needs.byHand: Hata does not know this system's package manager: install the {package} package yourself and try again.

error.disk.changed: The disks have changed since this window was opened. Close it and look again.
error.disk.inUse: The disk is in use, so Hata leaves it alone.
error.disk.folderTaken: There is already a folder with this name under /mnt that is in use or not empty. Pick another name.
error.disk.noPartitionTool: The program that writes partition tables is not installed.
error.disk.noFormatTool: The program that makes this file system is not installed.

error.disk.badFs: Hata does not work with this file system.
error.disk.tooBigForFat: FAT32 cannot be larger than 2 TB. Choose exFAT.
error.disk.noCheckTool: The program that checks this file system is not installed.
error.disk.noLabelTool: The program that names this file system is not installed.
error.disk.badLabel: This label has nothing the file system can carry. Type another one.
error.disk.labelFailed: The disk could not be renamed. {message}
error.disk.working: Another long operation — a copy, a move, a format or a check — is still running. Wait until it is done.
error.disk.noExfat: This system cannot open exFAT: its kernel has no driver for it.
error.disk.mountFailed: The disk could not be connected. {message} If it was unplugged without ejecting, check it: “Details”, then “Check”.
error.disk.notOurs: This folder was not connected by Hata, so it is not Hata's to disconnect.
error.disk.busy: Something is still using the folder. Stop the apps that keep files there and try again. {message}
error.disk.holds.data: The data folder lies on this disk. Move it in Settings → Apps first.
error.disk.holds.backups: The backups are kept on this disk. Choose another folder in Backups first.
error.disk.holds.state: Hata's own configuration lies on this disk.
error.disk.holds.share: A folder on this disk is shared over the network. Stop sharing it first.

error.settings.badStorage: The storage settings are not valid.
error.disk.noSmart: This disk gives no SMART data, so it cannot test itself.
error.disk.testFailed: The disk refused to start the self-test.

attention.smart.critical.title: Disk {disk} raised a critical warning
attention.smart.critical.text: Copy what matters off it now and replace it.

attention.smart.test.text: Copy what matters off it and replace it.

disks.tool.what: What it is: a small system package with the smartctl program, which asks a disk for its own health record (SMART).
disks.tool.why: What for: without it Hata shows the disks, but cannot tell a healthy one from one that is wearing out, show their temperature or warn you before a disk fails.
disks.tool.how: What the button does: runs the command below on this server. On Debian and Ubuntu the package also starts its own background service, smartd. Hata installs nothing until you press it.
disks.tool.byHand: Hata does not know this system's package manager: install the smartmontools package yourself, and the disks' health will show up here.
shares.title: Shared folders
shares.lead: Folders of this server that open on a computer or a phone like a disk of their own — in Explorer, Finder or a file manager, without the browser.
shares.none: Nothing is shared yet. Share a folder here, or from its menu in Files.
shares.error: The last change was not applied. {message}
shares.col.name: Folder
shares.name: Name on the network
shares.nameHint: Letters, digits, spaces, dots and hyphens, up to 40 characters.
shares.found.both: No address has to be typed where the network is browsed: this server shows up by itself as “{name}” — under “Network” in Explorer on Windows, in the sidebar of Finder and in the Files app of a phone.
shares.found.windows: On Windows no address has to be typed: this server shows up by itself as “{name}” under “Network” in Explorer. Finder and phones find it by themselves only when the name on the home network ends in .local and is on.
shares.found.browse: In Finder and in the Files app of a phone no address has to be typed: this server shows up by itself as “{name}”.
shares.found.error: Windows is not told of this server, so it does not appear under “Network” there: {message}
shares.how.title: How to open them
shares.how.windows: Windows: type {address} into the address bar of Explorer.
shares.how.mac: macOS: Finder → Go → Connect to Server, then {address}.
shares.how.phone: Phone: “Connect to Server” in the Files app of an iPhone, or a file manager that knows SMB on Android — with the same address.
shares.tool.what: What it is: the system package that serves folders over SMB, the network protocol of Windows — the one Windows, macOS, Linux, phones and TVs all understand.
shares.tool.why: What for: without it the folders of this server are reached only through the browser. With it they open like a network disk.
shares.tool.how: What the button does: runs the command below on this server. The package starts its own background service, which listens on port 445. From then on Samba is set up by Hata: its configuration is written from these settings, and the one that was there is kept as smb.conf.before-hata.
shares.tool.byHand: Hata does not know this system's package manager: install the samba package yourself, and sharing will show up here.
shares.tool.note: Sharing needs Samba, which is not installed on this server yet.
error.shares.protected: This folder cannot be shared: it is the system's own or holds Hata's configuration.
error.shares.notFound: There is no such shared folder.
error.shares.badName: A name on the network is letters, digits, spaces, dots and hyphens, up to 40 characters.
error.shares.nameTaken: Another folder is already shared as “{name}”.
error.shares.badPath: A folder with %, a backslash or a line break in its path cannot be shared.
error.shares.tooMany: No more than {max} folders can be shared.
shares.guestHint: Whoever is on the home network. Windows 11 and recent Windows 10 refuse to connect without a password until that is allowed in Windows itself.
shares.notReadyHint: signs in to Hata once more first
shares.users.title: Who connects
shares.users.lead: People connect with the name and the password they sign in to Hata with. Samba has to keep a password itself, and learns it when it is typed into Hata — so someone who has not signed in since sharing was set up signs in to Hata once, and the folders open for them.
shares.users.note: Two-factor sign-in and passkeys do not reach here: over the network the password alone opens a folder.
shares.users.notReady: after the next sign-in to Hata
error.shares.badAccess: Access is “none”, “read” or “write”, for users that exist.
agents.title: Access keys
agents.lead: An AI agent — Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor or another program that speaks MCP — can look after this server for you: say why an app is down, update it, install a new one. It connects with a key made here instead of your password, and may do only what the key's level allows.
agents.none: No keys yet: nothing but the people who sign in can reach this server.
agents.new.lead: One key per agent or computer: then each can be taken away on its own.
agents.new.name: Name
agents.new.nameHint: What the agent does is written into the activity log under this name.
agents.level.read.hint: Sees the state of the server, the apps and their logs, backups, disks and the store. Changes nothing.
agents.level.operate.hint: Also starts, stops, restarts and updates apps, installs apps from the store and takes snapshots.
agents.level.full.hint: Also changes compose files, installs apps from a compose file, removes apps and restores snapshots. An app can be given the whole machine through its compose file — give this level only to an agent you would trust with an administrator's password.
agents.levels.title: The levels
agents.never: No key of any level reaches users and passwords, the keys themselves, files, the terminal or Hata's own settings. Values in compose files that look like secrets (passwords, tokens) are hidden from keys below “Everything”. Logs are shown as they are — and whatever an agent reads is sent to the company whose model it runs on.
agents.remove.title: Remove the key “{name}”?
agents.remove.lead: The agent that uses it loses access at once. This cannot be undone — a new key has to be made and given to the agent.
agents.how.title: Where agents connect
agents.how.address: The address of the MCP server (Streamable HTTP). The key goes in the header “Authorization: Bearer <key>”; what to paste into the agent is shown when a key is made.
agents.how.plain: This page is open over plain HTTP: on the way to the server a key can be read by whoever is on the same network. Fine at home; from outside, use the HTTPS address.
agents.made.title: The key “{name}” is ready
agents.made.lead: Copy it now: it is shown only this once, and Hata keeps no copy of it.
agents.made.claudeHint: Run this command on the computer where Claude Code is.
agents.made.configHint: The same as an entry of the agent's MCP settings (the file is usually called mcp.json or .mcp.json).
activity.agents.create: Access key “{target}” made for an agent
error.agents.badName: Give the key a name, up to 40 characters.
error.agents.nameTaken: There is already a key with this name.
error.agents.tooMany: There are 20 keys already. Remove one that is not used.
error.agents.notFound: There is no such key any more.
assistant.title: Assistant
assistant.lead: Ask in your own words — “why is Jellyfin down?”, “what takes up the disk?”, “update everything” — and the assistant looks at the server with the same tools an outside agent has, and acts. What only looks, it does at once; every change it shows you first, and nothing changes until you press “Run”. Hata has no model of its own: name the one to ask.
assistant.provider.openai: OpenAI-compatible: OpenAI, OpenRouter, Ollama and others
assistant.url.openai: Leave empty for OpenAI's own. A model on your own machine: Ollama is “http://<address>:11434/v1”, LM Studio “http://<address>:1234/v1”. The model must be able to call tools.
assistant.keyHint: Kept on the server next to the other secrets and never shown again. A server of your own may need none.
assistant.keySaved: saved — type a new one to replace it
assistant.modelHint: The model's name as the provider calls it. “Show the models” asks the provider what this key may use.
assistant.modelsFound: Models found: {n} — pick one in the field
assistant.level.asks: Every change is shown to you before it runs.
assistant.level.full: Every change is shown to you before it runs. At this level the assistant reads compose files whole, with the passwords in them.
assistant.privacy: What the assistant reads to answer you — the state of the server and the apps, their logs, compose files — is sent to the provider of the model. With a model on your own machine it stays at home. The chats are kept on this server, thirty of the latest for each administrator.
assistant.notSet: The assistant is not set up yet.
assistant.notSetHint: It needs a model to think with: an API key of Anthropic or OpenAI, or a model on your own machine.
assistant.helloHint: I see the apps, their logs, the disks and the backups, and can start, stop, update and install apps. Every change I show you first.
assistant.start.health: Is everything all right on the server?
assistant.placeholder: Ask about the server or an app…
assistant.whyDown: Why is the app “{title}” ({app}) not working? Find the cause and say what to do.
assistant.tool.overview: look at the state of the server
assistant.tool.app_diagnose: find out what is wrong with {app}
assistant.tool.job_get: see how the operation is going
assistant.tool.app_install_compose: install the app {app} from a compose file
assistant.tool.app_remove: remove the app {app} (its data stays on disk)
assistant.tool.app_remove.data: remove the app {app} together with its data
assistant.tool.backup_restore: put {app} back to the snapshot {snapshot} — what was written since is lost
error.assistant.bad: These settings cannot be saved as they are.
error.assistant.badUrl: The address must start with http:// or https://.
error.assistant.notSet: The assistant is not set up: Settings → Assistant.
error.assistant.noChat: There is no such chat any more.
error.assistant.noCall: This action is not waiting for an answer any more.
error.assistant.busy: The assistant is still working on the previous message.
error.assistant.key: The provider did not accept the API key.
error.assistant.rate: The provider says there were too many requests, or the account's limit is reached. Try again later.
error.assistant.unreachable: The provider of the model could not be reached. Check the address and the server's internet.
error.assistant.model: The provider does not know this model or this address.
error.assistant.refused: The provider of the model refused the request.
error.approvals.gone: This request is not waiting any more: it was answered, or ten minutes have passed.
error.oauth.gone: This request to connect has lapsed or was answered already. Start connecting again in the program.
agents.how.signin: A connector that has nowhere to paste a key — one on claude.ai, for example — is given this address alone. It sends you to this server to sign in and to say what it may do; what it gets is listed above with the keys and is removed the same way. A service on the internet reaches the server only at an HTTPS address open to the internet.
activity.agents.connect: The connector “{target}” was let in as an agent
connect.asks: “{name}” asks to look after this server
connect.lead: A program wants to connect to this server as an AI agent: to see the state of the server and its apps and, as far as you allow below, to manage them. It gets no password — only an access that you can take away in Settings → Agents.
connect.whereHint: After you allow, the browser is sent there with the answer. The name above is what the program calls itself — this address is what tells who it really is.
connect.where.app: the app that opens “{scheme}://” links on this device
connect.warn: Allow only what you have started yourself, just now, in that program. If this page opened by itself or from a link somebody sent you, decline.
connect.name: What to call it
connect.nameHint: The name it has in Settings → Agents and in the activity log. Say which computer or chat it is, so that you can tell it from the others later.
connect.passwordHint: To confirm that it is you who lets the agent in.
connect.done: Allowed. You can go back to the program now.
connect.declined: Declined: the program got no access.
connect.adminOnly: Only an administrator of this server can let an agent in.
agents.confirm: Ask me each time before it removes an app, restores a snapshot or replaces a compose file. The agent's call then waits until an administrator allows it — on Hata's page or from the notification.
approvals.title: The agent “{agent}” asks for your word
approvals.hint: The agent's call is not run until an administrator allows it. A request nobody answers lapses in ten minutes, and a word is good for this one call only.
approvals.what.app_remove: remove the app “{app}” (its data stays on disk)
approvals.what.app_remove.data: remove the app “{app}” together with its data
approvals.what.backup_restore: put the app “{app}” back to the snapshot {snapshot} — what was written since is lost
approvals.what.app_compose_set: replace the compose file of the app “{app}”
activity.agents.asks: The key “{target}” now asks before it destroys
activity.agents.asksNot: The key “{target}” no longer asks before it destroys
app.newerImage: a newer one is in the registry
images.title: Image updates
images.checkHint: Once a day Hata asks the registries whether the tags your apps use point at newer images. Nothing is downloaded: an app with a newer image gets a mark, and “Update images” lights up on its page.
images.status: Checked {when} · images: {asked} · with a newer version: {newer}
images.autoHint: Every day at the set time the running apps with newer images are updated, as if “Update images” was pressed: a snapshot of the app's data first (when that is on in Backups), then the new images and a restart. A stopped app is left alone. An update that failed shows up in “Needs attention”.
error.settings.badImages: The image update settings are not valid.
network.lead: The network interfaces of the server. Changing an address goes through NetworkManager, and every change is on trial: unless this page reaches the server again in time, the previous settings come back by themselves.
network.addressHint: With the size of the network after the slash: 192.168.1.10/24.
network.dnsHint: Up to three addresses. Empty — the ones the router gives, or none with a fixed address.
network.handoverHint: The system's own service sets this interface up. To change it here, hand it over to NetworkManager first — with the address it has now.
network.needsTool: The system's own service sets this interface up. Changing it here needs NetworkManager.
network.readOnly: Hata only shows this interface: it is set up by something it does not change.
network.stopped: NetworkManager is installed but not running.
network.needs.why: Hata changes addresses, and later Wi-Fi and modems, through NetworkManager — the standard Linux service for it. Installing it changes nothing by itself: interfaces the system already set up stay as they are until you hand them over.
network.change.title: Address of {nic}
network.autoHint: DHCP: the router gives the address. The server may then be found at another address than now.
network.manualHint: The address stays the same whatever the router does.
network.handover.title: Hand {nic} over to NetworkManager
network.handover.lead: The interface keeps the address it has now; what changes is which service looks after it.
network.handover.how: Hata makes the NetworkManager profile “hata-{nic}” and tells the system's service (systemd-networkd, netplan's files stay untouched) to leave {nic} alone: a file in /etc/systemd/network, a udev rule, and the boot no longer waits for it there. The connection drops for a second or two.
network.trial.promise: On trial for {n} seconds: if this page does not reach the server again in that time, the previous settings come back by themselves.
network.trial.title: The change of {nic} is on trial
network.trial.lead: Looking whether the server is still reached.
network.trial.checking: As soon as this page reaches the server, the change is kept. Otherwise the previous settings come back.
network.trial.moved: The server should now be at {address}. This page cannot follow it there — open the link to keep the change. If it does not open, wait: the old address comes back.
network.trial.back: The server was not reached in time: the previous settings are back
error.network.badAddress: The address must look like 192.168.1.10/24 and be an address a machine can have.
error.network.badGateway: The gateway must be another address of the same network.
error.network.badDns: DNS is up to three addresses like 192.168.1.1.
error.network.badMethod: Choose where the address comes from.
error.network.pending: Another change is on trial. Wait until it is kept or taken back.
error.network.nothingPending: There is no change on trial any more.
error.network.notOurs: This interface is not looked after by NetworkManager.
error.network.cannotHandOver: This interface cannot be handed over.
error.network.noNic: There is no such interface any more.
activity.network.rolledBack: A network change of {target} was not confirmed and was taken back
network.handover.howIfupdown: Hata makes the NetworkManager profile “hata-{nic}” and comments {nic} out in /etc/network/interfaces (the file as it was is kept next to it as interfaces.before-hata). The connection drops for a few seconds; with an address from the router, the router may give another one.
wifi.title: Wi-Fi networks of {nic}
wifi.needs.what: The program for Wi-Fi is not installed
wifi.needs.why: NetworkManager joins Wi-Fi networks through wpa_supplicant, the standard Linux program for Wi-Fi passwords and encryption. Without it the adapter is seen and cannot be used. NetworkManager is restarted after the install; what it has connected stays connected.
error.network.notWifi: This is not a Wi-Fi interface.
error.network.badSsid: This is not a network name.
error.network.wifiGone: This network is no longer in reach.
error.network.badWifiPassword: A Wi-Fi password is 8 to 63 Latin letters, digits and signs.
error.network.wifiWrongPassword: The network did not let the server in — most likely the password is wrong.
network.modemHint: A USB modem or a phone that shares its connection: it gives the server an address by itself. Its SIM, PIN and operator are set up on the modem's own page (http://{gateway}, from the server). A spare way takes over when the main one goes away — the cable pulled out, the router off; with “Check that the internet works” on, also when the router is on and its internet is down.
error.network.badRole: Choose the main way, a spare one or none.
activity.network.role.backup: {target} is a spare way to the internet
activity.network.role.off: {target} is not used for the internet
hotspot.title: The server's own Wi-Fi
hotspot.lead: The Wi-Fi adapter becomes an access point: phones and computers join the server's own network, reach Hata and the apps there, and go to the internet through the server — through whatever is its main way, a USB modem too.
hotspot.leaves: The adapter does one thing at a time: it leaves {ssid}.
hotspot.name: Network name
hotspot.passwordHint: 8 to 63 Latin letters, digits and signs.
hotspot.band24: 2.4 GHz — reaches further, every device knows it
hotspot.bandHint: Not every adapter can be an access point at 5 GHz; if it does not start, take 2.4.
hotspot.scan: Point a phone's camera at the code to join.
hotspot.needs.what: The program that hands out addresses is not installed
hotspot.needs.why: Whoever joins the access point needs an address and a name service; NetworkManager starts dnsmasq for that, on this network only.
error.network.noAp: This adapter cannot be an access point.
error.network.hotspotOnlyWay: This Wi-Fi network is the server's only connection: as an access point it would leave it, and Hata would be out of reach. Connect a cable first.
error.network.hotspotFailed: The access point did not start: {message}
wifi.endsHotspot: The adapter does one thing at a time: joining a network turns the access point “{ssid}” off.
network.shareHint: The server becomes the router on this port: whatever is plugged in — a computer, a switch with several — gets an address from it and goes to the internet through the server's main way. For a spare port, not the one the server itself is reached by.
error.network.shareMain: The internet comes in through this interface — it cannot be given out through it too.
network.checkHint: Every minute NetworkManager asks for a small page ({url}) through each way to the internet. A way that gets no answer is marked and moved behind the ones that work — so a spare way takes over also when the router is on and its internet is down, and gives the place back when it returns.
activity.network.check.on: The check of the internet turned on
activity.network.check.off: The check of the internet turned off
attention.internet.main.title: The internet goes through the spare way
attention.internet.main.text: {nic} is connected but reaches no internet, so {other} carries it. The place is given back by itself when the internet returns.
attention.internet.spare.title: The spare way has no internet
attention.internet.spare.text: {nic} is connected but reaches no internet: it will not help when the main way goes. A modem may be out of money or signal.
attention.internet.none.title: The server has no internet
attention.internet.none.text: {nic} is connected and reaches no internet, and there is no other way that does. The home network still works.
network.shareAddressHint: With the size of the network: 192.168.50.1/24. Whoever is plugged in gets an address of the same network. Empty — NetworkManager picks one (10.42.x.1/24).
network.address6Hint: With the size of the network after the slash: 2001:db8::10/64.
network.dns6Hint: Up to three IPv6 addresses. Empty — the ones the router gives.
network.handback.title: Give {nic} back
network.handback.lead: The interface goes back to what set it up before Hata took it: {service}. From then on Hata only shows it.
network.handback.how: Hata removes its files for {nic} (in /etc/systemd/network, the udev rule) and the NetworkManager profile “hata-{nic}”. The system's service then sets the interface up by its own files — with the address written there, which may differ from the one it has now. The connection drops for a few seconds.
network.handback.howIfupdown: Hata puts the lines of {nic} back into /etc/network/interfaces and removes the NetworkManager profile “hata-{nic}”. The interface gets the address written in that file, which may differ from the one it has now. The connection drops for a few seconds.
wifi.otherLead: For a network that hides its name and so is not in the list: type the name exactly, capitals included.
wifi.otherPasswordHint: Empty — a network without a password.
hotspot.restarts: The access point starts anew with these settings: whoever has joined is dropped and joins again.
hotspot.channelHint: Worth setting when the neighbours' networks crowd the one picked. Which channels are allowed depends on the adapter and the country; if it does not start, leave the choice to the adapter.
hotspot.ownAddress: The server's address in this network
hotspot.ownAddressHint: With the size of the network: 192.168.50.1/24. Whoever joins gets an address of the same network. Empty — NetworkManager picks one (10.42.0.1/24).
error.network.badShareAddress: The address must look like 192.168.50.1/24, with a network of /16 to /28.
error.network.addressTaken: The server is already on this network: {nic} has {address}. Take another one.
error.network.badAddress6: The IPv6 address must look like 2001:db8::10/64.
error.network.badGateway6: The IPv6 gateway must be another address, like fe80::1.
error.network.badDns6: IPv6 DNS is up to three addresses like 2606:4700:4700::1111.
error.network.badChannel: There is no such channel in this band.
error.network.notHanded: Hata did not hand this interface over, so there is nobody to give it back to.
activity.network.givenBack: {target} given back to the system's service
backup.files.title: Snapshot of {title}
backup.files.reading: Reading the archive… A large one takes a while the first time.
backup.files.sureLead: Each of these is replaced with what it was at {time}; what lies there now is lost. Inside a folder outside AppData nothing is deleted — the snapshot's files are written over the present ones. {title} is stopped meanwhile and started again.
backup.folders.title: What a snapshot of {title} holds
backup.folders.alwaysHint: The compose file, the app's Docker volumes and its folders in AppData.
backup.folders.otherHint: Folders the app uses outside AppData — media, documents. A chosen one is copied whole into every snapshot, so mind its size against the free space and the number of snapshots kept; the app is stopped for as long as the copying takes. At a restore such a folder is not emptied first: the snapshot's files are written over what is there.
backup.folders.none: The app uses no folders outside AppData.
backup.folders.unknown: size not counted — too large to count quickly, or not there
backup.folders.never: not copied: a system folder, or the whole data folder
error.backup.badFolder: This folder cannot go into a snapshot.
error.backup.noSuchFile: There is no such file in the snapshot.
array.title: Protection from a disk failure
array.lead: One disk holds parity for the others (SnapRAID): when any one disk dies, what it held is computed back from the rest. The disks stay ordinary disks with ordinary files. The parity is as fresh as the last sync — what was added or changed since is not protected yet — so it suits media and backups, not what apps write all day.
array.needs.what: What is missing: snapraid, a small system package that computes and checks the parity.
array.needs.why: What for: it is the whole of this protection. Installing it changes nothing by itself: nothing runs until you choose the disks.
array.needsDisks: It takes at least two disks connected by Hata for good: one for parity, one or more with data. Format them as ext4 above.
array.turnedOn: Protection is set up. Start the first sync when the disks hold what you want protected.
array.runningHint: It may take hours on large disks. The page can be closed; a run that is stopped goes on from where it was next time.
array.waitingNew: new or changed files, not protected yet: {n}
array.scheduleScrub: sync every night at {time}, a check on Sundays
array.appDataOut: left out — the backups cover it
array.missingHint: Nothing is synced while a disk of the array is away, so what the parity knows stays as it was. If the disk is dead: disconnect its folder above, format the new disk under the same folder name, and press “Recover…” next to it.
array.diskEmptyHint: Every file the parity knows on this disk is gone — a new disk in the place of a dead one looks exactly like this. The sync is stopped, so the parity still holds those files.
array.emptyOnPurpose: It was emptied on purpose — sync
array.parityLost: The parity on {disk} is gone or cut short
array.parityLostHint: A new disk in the place of the parity disk looks like this. Nothing is lost while the data disks are well — the parity is computed anew from them, which reads every disk whole.
array.errorsHint: A check read data that is not what was written — a disk is going bad, or a file was damaged silently. The parity can put it right; look at the health of the disks above too.
array.held: The sync is waiting: {n} files are gone since the last one
array.heldHint: That is more than the limit, and a sync would make the parity forget them. If they were deleted by mistake, they can still be brought back.
array.syncAnyway: They were deleted on purpose — sync
array.failed: The last sync did not go through: {message}
array.how: Choose one disk for parity and the disks to protect. The parity disk must be at least as large as the largest protected one, and holds nothing else of Hata's.
array.parityDiskHint: Its room goes to the parity file; files of your own are better kept elsewhere.
array.cannot.merged: part of a merged folder — cannot hold parity
array.cannot.holds: the data folder, the backups or a shared folder lie here — cannot hold parity
array.appDataHint: Off by default. Apps write there all day, so much of it would always be newer than the parity, and files brought back lose their owners — which databases do not forgive. The backups are what covers AppData.
array.limit: Wait when more files are gone than
array.scrub: Check a part of the array every Sunday
array.scrubHint: Reads an eighth of the data and compares it with what was written, so damage is found while it can still be repaired.
array.anew: With other disks than before, the parity there is of no use: it is removed, and the first sync computes it from scratch. Until then nothing is protected.
array.offLead: Nothing is synced or checked any more. Your files are not touched.
array.offWipeHint: It only takes room once the protection is off; without it, turning the protection on again starts from scratch.
array.recoverLead: Every file the parity knows on this disk and that is not there now is computed back. Files that are there are not touched.
array.recoverHow: For a disk that died: the new one has to be connected as {disk} — formatted under the same folder name — and the others must be in place. It takes as long as reading all the disks.
array.recoverOwners: The parity keeps the files, not whose they were: what comes back takes the owner of the disk's top folder and is readable by everybody.
error.array.busy: Something is running on the array already. Wait for it or stop it.
error.array.off: The protection is not set up.
error.array.badDisks: Choose a parity disk and at least one other disk to protect.
error.array.parityMerged: A disk of a merged folder cannot hold parity.
error.array.parityHolds: The data folder, the backups or a shared folder lie on this disk — it cannot hold parity.
error.array.parityTooSmall: The parity disk must be at least as large as the largest protected disk.
error.array.missing: Not connected: {disks}. All the other disks have to be in place.
error.disk.holds.array: This disk is part of the protection from a disk failure. Take it out of there first.
attention.array.errors.title: Damaged data on the disks
attention.array.errors.text: A check of the array found {n} damaged blocks. The parity can repair them: Settings → Storage.
attention.array.diskEmpty.title: {disk} has lost everything it held
attention.array.diskEmpty.text: The sync is stopped, so the parity still knows those files and they can be recovered.
attention.array.parityLost.title: The parity is gone
attention.array.parityLost.text: The parity file on {disk} is missing or cut short. Until it is computed anew, a disk failure is not covered.
attention.array.held.title: The parity sync is waiting for you
attention.array.held.text: {n} files are gone since the last sync. Bring them back or say it was meant: Settings → Storage.
attention.array.failed.title: The parity sync did not go through
activity.array.on: Protection from a disk failure turned on
activity.array.changed: Protection from a disk failure changed
activity.array.off: Protection from a disk failure turned off
activity.array.held: The parity sync is waiting: too many files are gone
activity.array.sync.failed: The parity sync did not go through
activity.array.errors: A check of the array found damaged data
activity.array.repair.done: Damaged data repaired from the parity
activity.array.repair.failed: Damaged data could not be repaired
activity.array.fix.done: Files brought back from the parity
activity.array.fix.failed: Not every file could be brought back from the parity
activity.array.diskEmpty: {target} has lost everything it held: the parity sync is stopped
attention.docker.missing.title: Docker is not installed
attention.docker.missing.text: Apps run in Docker; without it nothing from the store can be installed. Hata installs nothing by itself — press the button.
attention.docker.stopped.title: Docker is not running
attention.docker.stopped.text: It is installed, but does not answer, so the apps are down. {message}
docker.title: Docker
docker.what: What is missing: Docker Engine with the compose plugin — the program every app here runs in.
docker.why: What for: an app is a compose file that Docker runs. Without Docker Hata still shows the server, its files, disks and network, but cannot install or start an app.
docker.how: This is Docker's own installer: it adds Docker's package repository for this system and installs the engine. It takes a minute or two and needs the internet; Docker then starts with the system.
error.docker.missing: Docker is not installed. Install it from the home page, under “Needs attention”.
attention.disk.new.title: A disk nothing uses yet: {disk}, {size}
attention.disk.new.text: It can be formatted for files, or connected as it is, in Settings → Storage — or waved away there.
attention.disk.usb.title: Plugged in: {disk}, {size}
attention.disk.usb.text: It holds files. They can be copied onto the server — all of them, or the folders and files you choose.
activity.historyLead: What happened on this server and who did it, newest first.
activity.start: That is where the history begins.
activity.noMatch: Nothing like that among what is loaded.
copyin.title: Copy from {disk}
copyin.lead: What the disk holds is copied onto the server; nothing on the disk itself is changed.
copyin.allHint: Untick to choose folders and files; a folder opens when its name is pressed.
copyin.nothing: There is nothing on this disk that can be opened.
copyin.subHint: Empty — straight into the folder chosen. A name that is taken gets “(2)”.
activity.app.copyin.done: Files copied from a plugged-in disk
activity.app.copyin.failed: Copying from a plugged-in disk failed
tools.lead: The programs of the system Hata relies on: what each is for and whether it is here. Hata installs and removes nothing by itself — each is installed or removed by its button, with the command shown.
tools.docker.what: Every app runs in it: an app is a compose file that Docker runs. Without it nothing can be installed or started.
tools.samba.what: Serves the folders shared over the network (SMB) to Windows, macOS and phones. Hata writes its whole configuration.
tools.smartmontools.what: Asks a disk for its own health log (SMART): healthy, wearing out or failing, and its temperature.
tools.fdisk.what: Writes a disk's partition table (sfdisk) when a disk is formatted whole.
tools.e2fsprogs.what: Makes, checks and names ext4 file systems, and closes the empty folder of a disk that is away.
tools.dosfstools.what: Makes, checks and names FAT32 — the file system old devices read.
tools.exfatprogs.what: Makes, checks and names exFAT — the file system of sticks and disks that go between devices.
tools.ntfs-3g.what: Makes, checks and names NTFS, the file system of Windows, and reads and writes it on systems whose kernel cannot do that by itself.
tools.mergerfs.what: Shows several disks as one folder; the files stay ordinary files on each disk.
tools.snapraid.what: Computes and checks parity, so that what a dead disk held can be computed back from the others.
tools.network-manager.what: Changes the server's network: addresses, Wi-Fi, an access point, the ways to the internet. Without it Hata only shows the interfaces.
tools.wpasupplicant.what: Wi-Fi passwords and encryption: NetworkManager joins networks through it.
tools.dnsmasq-base.what: Hands out addresses to whoever joins the server's access point or a port that gives the internet out.
tools.openssh-client.what: Sends the second copy of the backups to another machine (sftp) and makes Hata's own key for it.
tools.ntfs-3g.builtIn: The kernel of this system reads and writes NTFS by itself (the ntfs3 driver), and Hata connects NTFS disks through it.
tools.removeLead: The program is removed from the system. Its settings and data stay where they are, so installing it again picks up where it was.
tools.removeDocker: Every app stops and stays down until Docker is installed again. The apps' compose files, their data, the images and the volumes are not touched.
tools.holds.base: Part of the system itself, used by more than Hata — it is not removed from here.
tools.holds.shares: Folders are shared over the network through it. To remove it, stop sharing them first.
tools.holds.array: The protection from a disk failure runs on it. To remove it, turn the protection off first.
tools.holds.merged: A merged folder is made with it. To remove it, disconnect the merged folder first.
tools.holds.network: It holds a network interface of the server up — removing it now could cut the server off. Give the interfaces back to the system and leave the Wi-Fi network first.
tools.holds.wifi: The Wi-Fi connection or the access point runs through it. Leave the network or turn the access point off first.
tools.holds.hotspot: It hands out addresses on the access point or on a port that gives the internet out. Turn that off first.
tools.holds.ntfs: An NTFS disk is connected through it. Disconnect the disk first.
error.tools.notPackage: It was not installed as a package of this system, so Hata cannot remove it.
error.tools.holds.base: Part of the system itself, used by more than Hata — it is not removed from here.
error.tools.holds.shares: Folders are shared over the network through it. To remove it, stop sharing them first.
error.tools.holds.array: The protection from a disk failure runs on it. To remove it, turn the protection off first.
error.tools.holds.merged: A merged folder is made with it. To remove it, disconnect the merged folder first.
error.tools.holds.network: It holds a network interface of the server up — removing it now could cut the server off. Give the interfaces back to the system and leave the Wi-Fi network first.
error.tools.holds.wifi: The Wi-Fi connection or the access point runs through it. Leave the network or turn the access point off first.
error.tools.holds.hotspot: It hands out addresses on the access point or on a port that gives the internet out. Turn that off first.
error.tools.holds.ntfs: An NTFS disk is connected through it. Disconnect the disk first.
